overview: Demant A/S is a Danish hearing-healthcare group that develops, manufactures and sells hearing aids (Oticon, Bernafon, Philips), owns and operates one of the world's largest networks of hearing care clinics (4,500+ clinics in 25+ countries, including the German KIND chain), and is the global leader in audiometric and balance diagnostic equipment (Interacoustics, Amplivox, MedRx). Following the completed divestments of its Communications/headset business (EPOS, closed January 2026) and its hearing implants business (cochlear implants to Cochlear in May 2024; bone-anchored solutions to Impilo in March 2026), Demant is now a pure-play hearing-health company operating three segments: Hearing Aids, Hearing Care and Diagnostics. It serves customers in 130+ countries with roughly 44% of revenue from Europe and 39% from North America, and manufactures primarily in Poland and Mexico.

business_model.summary: A vertically integrated hearing-health model: Demant earns a high-margin wholesale manufacturing profit on hearing aids (77.1% group gross margin in H1 2026) and then captures the retail dispensing margin again through its own 4,500+ clinics. Roughly 21-24% of Hearing Aids revenue is internal, sold to its own Hearing Care arm and eliminated on consolidation. Revenue is largely transactional (device sales, ~4-5 year replacement cycle) rather than subscription, but is highly repeatable given the demographic pull and the clinic relationship, and is supplemented by recurring Diagnostics service/consumables income.

revenue_streams.name: Hearing Aids (external wholesale revenue)
revenue_streams.note: FY2025 external revenue DKK 9,841m of DKK 12,473m total including internal sales. Organic growth 0% in FY2025 external, but accelerated to +9% external / +12% total organic in H1 2026 on Oticon Zeal.

revenue_streams.name: Hearing Care (owned retail clinics)
revenue_streams.note: FY2025 revenue DKK 10,724m, now the largest reported segment. +6% organic and +23% acquisitive in H1 2026 on the KIND deal. Largest single driver of acquisitive growth.

revenue_streams.name: Diagnostics (audiometric & balance equipment)
revenue_streams.note: FY2025 revenue DKK 2,406m, +1% organic FY2025 recovering to +6% organic in H1 2026. Global market leader; growing service/consumables annuity on an installed instrument base.

business_model.vertical_integration: Retail ownership is the strategic core of the model. Owning the audiologist channel (a) captures the dispensing margin on top of the wholesale margin, roughly doubling revenue per fitted device; (b) guarantees shelf space for Oticon/Bernafon/Philips product in a market where the majority of clinics globally are still independently owned and can switch brands freely; (c) provides a defensive hedge against wholesale ASP pressure from consolidating managed-care buyers; and (d) supplies proprietary demand data. It also raises the strategic stakes: retail roll-up is capital hungry, converts equity into goodwill, and lowers group gross margin mix while raising absolute EBIT. Management explicitly frames 'participate in consolidation of distribution' as one of three strategic choices, with a medium-term target of ~2% acquisitive growth p.a. on top of 6-8% organic.
business_model.customer_type: Mixed. B2B wholesale to independent hearing care professionals, large retail chains, and government tender channels (UK NHS, US Veterans Affairs); B2C through its own clinics; and B2B/institutional for Diagnostics (hospitals, ENT clinics, schools). Customer concentration is low at group level: the ten largest customers were ~11% of FY2025 consolidated revenue.
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2025: Europe 44%, North America 39%, Asia 9%, Pacific 5%, Rest of world 3%
business_model.implants_status: Exited entirely. The Neuro cochlear implant business was sold to Cochlear Limited (announced April 2022, completed 21 May 2024 at a zero headline price after the UK CMA blocked the bone-anchored portion). The remaining bone-anchored hearing systems business was sold to Swedish investment company Impilo and completed 31 March 2026. There is no longer a Hearing Implants segment; FY2025's DKK -823m discontinued-operations loss reflects non-cash balance-sheet adjustments and provisions on the EPOS and Oticon Medical exits.

competitive_position.market_position: One of the 'big five' manufacturers that together control the overwhelming majority of the global hearing aid market. Demant is generally the #1 or #2 player alongside Sonova. Global market context: roughly 13 million people fitted with ~23 million hearing aids in 2025; wholesale market value ~USD 7bn p.a., retail value ~USD 20bn p.a. excluding government channels; diagnostics ~USD 0.7bn p.a. where Demant is the outright global leader. In the key US Veterans Affairs channel Demant held an 18.9% unit share in Q4 2025.

moat_factors.description: Five players dominate a technically demanding, regulated market with a ~USD 7bn wholesale pool. New scale entrants are rare; the barrier is a combination of audiological IP, chip platforms, clinical validation, regulatory clearance and channel access.

DKK 1.4bn+ invested annually in R&D (DKK 1,401m FY2025) against a 2,600+ patent and design portfolio. Proprietary DNN/AI sound-processing platforms (Oticon Intent, the Sirius platform, and the dual-AI Oticon Reveal launched August 2026) require sustained multi-hundred-million-DKK spend that sub-scale players cannot match. R&D spend is roughly 6% of revenue and grew only 2% in H1 2026, showing the operating leverage on a fixed technology base.

4,500+ owned clinics guarantee distribution for own-brand product and capture the retail margin. This is the hardest asset for a competitor to replicate quickly because clinic acquisition is a slow, fragmented, price-competitive roll-up. KIND alone added ~650 clinics and 3,000 employees.

moat_factors.factor: Switching costs and the professional relationship
moat_factors.description: The end user is bound to the fitting audiologist by fitting software, service, counselling and lifelong aftercare rather than to the manufacturer brand. This protects the retail leg strongly but protects the wholesale leg only as long as Demant either owns the clinic or wins the independent audiologist's preference each cycle.

Oticon is a globally recognised premium audiology brand with 120+ years of heritage; multi-brand structure (Oticon premium, Bernafon and Philips value/alternative-channel) lets Demant address different price points and channels without cannibalising.

Medical-device classification, ISO 14971/ISO 27001 compliance, notified-body audits, and market-by-market reimbursement listings create real but surmountable barriers - and cut both ways, since reimbursement schemes can be changed against Demant.

A ~4-5 year replacement cycle over an installed base of 12.1m lives improved (FY2025, rising to 12.6m at H1 2026) creates a predictable repeat-purchase stream, though it is not contractual and can be delayed by macro conditions - exactly what happened in 2025.

weaknesses: The wholesale leg is exposed to product-cycle timing: FY2025 saw a genuine US market-share loss driven primarily by lower sales to one large US retailer that added suppliers, proving how quickly channel decisions can move the needle.

Structurally flat-to-negative ASP: management's own base case is flattish ASP long-term, with FY2025 ASP down 2% on geography and channel mix. Growth must therefore come from units, mix and acquisition, not price.
Growing dependence on acquisitive growth (10% of H1 2026 revenue growth versus 7% organic), which raises leverage and goodwill and makes reported growth less comparable.
Weak position in China, where the group has flat-to-negative growth and limited access to public/tender markets, and consistently challenging market dynamics across both Hearing Aids and Diagnostics.

Retail ownership dilutes group gross margin mix and adds fixed-cost operating leverage (distribution costs are DKK 10.9bn/year, the largest single cost line), making earnings more sensitive to volume shortfalls than a pure wholesaler.

growth_drivers: Demographics: WHO estimates one in five people live with some degree of hearing loss and over 400 million have moderate-to-severe loss that would benefit from treatment; roughly half of the structural 4-6% p.a. market growth is expected to come from ageing populations alone.

Penetration: fewer than 20% of people who would benefit from a hearing aid currently receive treatment, leaving a very long runway; the other half of structural market growth is expected from improving access and reduced stigma. Demant's own 2030 targets are 16m lives improved and 2m people hearing-tested annually (from 12.1m and 1.6m in FY2025).

Retail roll-up: continued consolidation of a highly fragmented global clinic market, targeting ~2% acquisitive growth p.a. Recent deals include KIND (~650 clinics, Germany), Ohrwerk (77 clinics, Germany), Amplifon's UK estate (~100 clinics, ~GBP 29m revenue) and Dansk Horecenter (36 clinics) - larger chains gain purchasing power and operating leverage.

Product cycle: Oticon Zeal (launched EUHA October 2025, US January 2026) drove the H1 2026 acceleration and delivered US commercial and VA share gains; Oticon Reveal, with dual Speech-AI/Context-AI processing, became orderable 24 August 2026 and carries the H2 2026 and 2027 growth case. Portfolio breadth extended via Verit (disposable battery), Play SI (paediatric), and Auracast/Google Fast Pair connectivity.

Cost programme: the February 2026 company-wide profitability initiative is running ahead of plan, now expected to add ~DKK 300m to FY2026 EBIT before special items (raised from ~DKK 250m), with the majority landing in H2.

Diagnostics recovery: the global leader in a USD 0.7bn market with a 4-6% structural growth rate, an expanding installed base driving service/consumables annuity, balance testing as an adjacency, and progress on Chinese regulatory approvals to access public markets.
Emerging markets: Rest of world and Latin America consistently outgrow the group; several small and medium-sized markets delivered good growth in H1 2026.
Premium mix and channel mix: gross margin reached 77.1% in H1 2026 (up 110bp YoY) on a stronger geography, channel and product mix, with management guiding above 77% for H2.

business.risk: OTC hearing aids and consumer-electronics disruption (Apple AirPods Pro)
business.description: US OTC hearing aids have been available since 2022, and Apple obtained FDA clearance for a hearing-aid feature on AirPods Pro 2 in October 2024 for mild-to-moderate loss. Demant's own FY2025 filing states that OTC 'impact on the prescription hearing aid market in the US remains limited' but concedes new form factors 'could pose a risk to the prescription hearing aid market, if successful'. VERIFICATION NOTE: searches through August 2026 returned no credible evidence of a measurable dent in prescription volumes attributable to Apple - the US commercial market weakness in 2025 was attributed by Demant to macro uncertainty and managed care, not OTC. Industry sources are ambiguous and largely generic; treat any claim that Apple has already damaged the market as unproven. The plausible medium-term effect is bifurcated: OTC may expand awareness and funnel first-time users into clinics, while compressing the entry-level price tier and, over time, anchoring consumer price expectations downward.

In a five-player oligopoly with a ~2-3 year platform cadence, losing a generation is expensive and slow to reverse. Demant's Q4 2025 VA unit share slipped to 18.9% specifically 'due to competitive launches'. Management explicitly warns the H2 2026 outlook assumes 'several competitors expected to launch new products in H2'. The current position is favourable (Zeal, Reveal) but that is precisely the point of maximum cyclical vulnerability going into the next round.

business.risk: Channel/customer concentration in wholesale despite low group concentration
business.description: Group ten-largest customers are only ~11% of revenue, but the FY2025 US share loss was traced to a single large retailer adding suppliers. Government channels (UK NHS, US VA) are similarly lumpy - NHS growth turned negative in H1 2026 on phasing.

Persistently challenging dynamics and limited access to public markets in both Hearing Aids and Diagnostics. Asia is only 9% of revenue so the earnings impact is contained, but it removes a growth engine peers may capture.

The September 2019 cyberattack cost DKK 550-650m of EBIT (net of ~DKK 100m insurance), roughly 15% of that year's operating profit, by halting production and distribution in Denmark and France. That is a demonstrated, quantified tail risk from a single IT event in a group whose value chain is highly centralised. Demant has since obtained ISO 27001 certification, runs annual NIST CSF maturity assessments and moved IT-security oversight to the audit committee in 2025 - mitigation, not elimination.

financial.description: The gearing multiple (NIBD/EBITDA before special items) hit 3.4x at end-2025 after the ~EUR 700m KIND acquisition, versus a stated medium-to-long-term target of 2.0-2.5x. It improved to 3.0x at 30 June 2026 and management expects it to 'drop further and slightly exceed the target' by end-2026, with a return to range within 18-24 months of the KIND close. NIBD was DKK 17,950m at H1 2026 against DKK 11,317m of equity. Because retail roll-up is a permanent strategic choice rather than a one-off, leverage and goodwill are structural features of the balance sheet, not transient. Total assets grew 20% in FY2025 essentially entirely on acquisition goodwill, creating persistent impairment risk if clinic economics deteriorate.

FY2026 guidance is explicitly 'Share buy-backs: None', reaffirmed at H1 2026, versus DKK 2,301m in 2024 and DKK 582m in 2025. Capital allocation policy subordinates buybacks to the 2.0-2.5x gearing target, so shareholder returns are on hold until deleveraging completes. Demant pays no ordinary dividend, so buybacks are the sole return-of-capital channel - meaning total shareholder return in 2026 depends entirely on multiple expansion and earnings growth.

Demant reports in DKK (effectively pegged to EUR) but earns heavily in USD and other currencies, with around two-thirds of invoices out of Denmark issued in currencies other than DKK or EUR. FX cut revenue by 3% and EBIT by ~DKK 50m in H1 2026, primarily on a weaker US dollar, and FY2026 guidance assumes ~DKK -125m FX drag on EBIT (improved from -200m). Translation risk from consolidating subsidiaries is explicitly NOT hedged; only commercial cash flows are, via forwards of up to 18 months (USD hedged 14 months at 635 as at 30 June 2026, versus 658 six months earlier).

Net financial items were DKK -731m in FY2025 and DKK -378m in H1 2026 on ~DKK 18bn of net debt. Only around 50% of next-twelve-months interest expense is fixed or hedged, leaving material floating exposure. Falling rates were a tailwind in 2025-26; a reversal would be a direct earnings drag.

regulatory.risk: US reimbursement and managed-care channel pressure
regulatory.description: A large part of US hearing aid purchases is covered by insurance, and Demant's own filing warns that 'the prevalence of large managed care organisations poses a risk to average selling prices... as volumes are increasingly consolidated among fewer players', with knock-on risk to customer loyalty and clinic fitting fees. This is not hypothetical: managed care showed negative growth through 2025 and again in both Q1 and Q2 2026, and US commercial market growth was flat in H1 2026 once managed care is included (2% excluding it). Medicare Advantage plan design changes are a live channel-economics risk.

regulatory.risk: Tariffs on Danish/Polish-manufactured devices into the US
regulatory.description: Demant manufactures in Poland and Mexico (with Denmark and France in the value chain) and sells ~39% of revenue into North America, so import duties are a genuine exposure. Realised impact has been small and is improving: FY2025 tariffs hurt the Diagnostics gross margin; FY2026 guidance originally assumed ~DKK -25m, but at H1 2026 management removed the assumption entirely, expecting a refund in H2 of previously paid US tariffs. Management notes it 'continuously evaluates alternative production locations'. The residual risk is a change in US trade policy, which management itself calls 'characterised by elevated uncertainty'.

Growth is materially dependent on government-set schemes - France's 100% Sante reform drove multi-year high single-digit unit growth, and UK NHS tenders swing regional growth in both directions. Adverse changes to reimbursement levels or distribution methods in France, Germany or the UK would directly hit volumes and ASP.

regulatory.risk: Medical device regulation and data privacy
regulatory.description: EU MDR, ISO 14971 risk-management and annual notified-body QMS inspections impose compliance cost; GDPR and health-data handling across 4,500 clinics adds breach exposure. Also subject to EU/US sanctions and export-control regimes (trade with Russia and Belarus has already halted).

Manufacturer ownership of retail is inherently a vertical-foreclosure question. The German Bundeskartellamt cleared the KIND/audifon deal unconditionally in November 2025, and the UK CMA has previously intervened in the sector (blocking the Cochlear/Oticon Medical BAHS transfer). Future large clinic acquisitions in concentrated markets may face longer reviews or remedies.

macro.risk: Consumer discretionary sensitivity and deferred purchases
macro.description: Despite the 'medical' framing, a large share of hearing aids is paid out of pocket, and 2025 proved the category is deferrable: global unit growth fell to 3% versus the 4-6% structural rate as macro uncertainty 'reduced the willingness to invest and resulted in delayed purchases'. Demant had to cut its FY2025 outlook twice. Demand is delayed rather than destroyed, but the timing risk is real.

macro.risk: Input costs and supply chain concentration
macro.description: Concentrated production in two main Polish sites plus Mexico creates single-region operational exposure, mitigated by proximity to main markets and safety stocks. A higher share of rechargeable devices raised production cost and pressured gross margin in FY2025. Semiconductors, batteries and specialist components come from highly specialised suppliers.
Twofold: directly through ~DKK 18bn of net debt of which roughly half is floating, and indirectly through the valuation of a leveraged, acquisition-driven compounder.

execution.description: The largest acquisition in Demant's history (KIND, ~EUR 700m, closed 1 December 2025) plus the Amplifon UK estate must be integrated while deleveraging. Early evidence is positive - KIND's expected FY2026 EBIT contribution was raised to DKK 325m from DKK 300m and integration is 'faster than expected' - but total special items for 2026 were also raised to DKK 400m from DKK 325m, with a further DKK 100m expected in 2027. The UK retail acquisition temporarily depressed H1 2026 EBIT during integration. Full KIND synergy realisation is not projected until end-2027.

execution.risk: Foundation control limits minority shareholder influence
execution.description: The William Demant Foundation, through William Demant Invest, held approximately 59% of share capital excluding treasury shares at end-2025 and has stated an intention to hold 55-60%. All shares are one class with one vote each, so there is no dual-class structure, but the Foundation nonetheless controls every ordinary shareholder vote. Free float is 41%, and average daily turnover fell to DKK 66m in 2025. Consequences for minorities: no realistic prospect of a takeover premium or activist campaign; board composition is effectively Foundation-determined (the Foundation's own board chair sits on Demant's nomination committee, and the Vice Chair Niels Jacobsen is CEO of William Demant Invest); only three of five shareholder-elected directors are classified independent; and the company complies with 38 of 40 Danish governance recommendations. The offsetting benefit is a genuinely long-term, patient owner that supports multi-year R&D and roll-up strategy and tolerates cyclical setbacks - historically a positive for a business whose value compounds over decades.

Soren Nielsen remains President & CEO (in post since 2017), but on 6 May 2026 he relinquished the concurrent role of President of Hearing Aids to focus solely on the group CEO role; Bassel Rifai joined as President of Hearing Aids effective 1 June 2026. Separately, Niels B. Christiansen, board chair since 2017, did not stand for re-election at the 5 March 2026 AGM. Two senior transitions in the same year at the top of the largest business area and the board is a modest execution risk, though the CEO continuity is the key stabiliser.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Structural growth of 4-6% p.a. in value in both hearing aids and diagnostic instruments, driven roughly half by demographics and half by improving access/penetration. The market undershot in 2025 (3% global unit growth, ~2% value) on macro uncertainty, and Demant's FY2026 assumption is a still-conservative 3-4% value growth, raised at H1 from 2-4%. H1 2026 actual came in at ~4% value growth - the high end of the company's expectation but only the low end of the structural range. Distribution continues to consolidate, favouring scale players.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate. Underlying need is non-discretionary and demographically driven, but purchase timing is discretionary and out-of-pocket exposure makes the category deferrable in downturns - clearly demonstrated by the 2025 slowdown and two guidance cuts. Not a defensive medtech in the pharma sense.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate. Direct: ~DKK 18bn NIBD with roughly half of next-twelve-months interest expense unhedged. Indirect: valuation of a leveraged roll-up compounder, and consumer financing of out-of-pocket purchases.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: High. Reports in DKK (effectively EUR-pegged) while earning heavily in USD, GBP, AUD, CAD, JPY and PLN. Around two-thirds of invoices out of Denmark are non-DKK/EUR. Transaction exposure is hedged up to 18 months; translation exposure is deliberately unhedged. FX reduced H1 2026 revenue 3% and EBIT ~DKK 50m; FY2026 guidance assumes ~DKK -125m EBIT impact.
key_input_costs: Clinic property leases and dispensing staff wages
macro_factors.regulatory_environment_trend: Broadly stable, with two divergent vectors: liberalisation at the low end (US OTC since 2022, FDA-cleared consumer-electronics hearing features) which pressures entry-level pricing while potentially expanding the funnel, and continued reliance on government/insurer reimbursement (NHS, VA, France's 100% Sante, German statutory cover) which is stable today but a single-decision risk in any given market.

recent_developments.event: Oticon Reveal became available to order - a new platform built on a dual-AI architecture (Speech AI plus Context AI), claimed to deliver a 60% stronger brain response versus prior approaches. It underpins the H2 2026 and 2027 growth case.

H1 2026 interim report published with an UPGRADED FY2026 outlook. Revenue DKK 12,913m (+15% reported, +7% organic, +10% acquisitive, -3% FX); gross margin 77.1% (+110bp); EBIT before special items DKK 2,134m (16.5% margin, +19% in local currencies); profit DKK 1,185m; FCF DKK 1,284m (+14%); gearing down to 3.0x from 3.4x. Beat consensus on both lines (EPS DKK 5.62 vs ~5.46 expected; revenue vs ~DKK 12.64bn expected); shares traded up toward the 52-week high around DKK 288-290.

Bassel Rifai joined as President of Hearing Aids and a member of the Executive Leadership Team. Announced 6 May 2026, this ends nine years in which CEO Soren Nielsen held the Hearing Aids presidency concurrently; Nielsen continues as President & CEO of the group.

Completed the divestment of the bone-anchored hearing solutions business (the residual Oticon Medical) to Stockholm-based investment company Impilo, finishing Demant's exit from implantable hearing solutions.
Annual general meeting: Niels B. Christiansen stepped down as Chair of the Board after eight years, having declined to stand for re-election. A revised Remuneration Policy was put to shareholders.

Launched a company-wide cost-saving and profitability initiative alongside FY2025 results, initially targeting ~DKK 250m of FY2026 EBIT benefit; raised to ~DKK 300m at H1 with ~DKK 100m already banked in H1, ahead of plan. Associated one-off severance/implementation costs raised to DKK 250m.

Closed the sale of EPOS (the Communications/enterprise headset business, ~USD 80m revenue) to ACCO Brands for EUR 7m plus up to EUR 3m contingent, completing the transition to a pure-play hearing-healthcare company.

Oticon Zeal went on sale in the US following its October 2025 EUHA launch and phased European rollout. It drove double-digit organic growth in North America and market-share gains in both the US commercial market and the VA channel in Q2 2026 - reversing the 2025 US share loss.

Closed the acquisition of KIND (Germany, ~650 clinics, ~3,000 employees, plus manufacturer audifon) for ~EUR 700m - the largest acquisition in Demant's history. Bundeskartellamt cleared it unconditionally on 19 November 2025. Took the clinic network above 4,500 and the gearing multiple to 3.4x.

FY2025 results: revenue DKK 22,971m (+2% organic), EBIT before special items DKK 3,960m (17.2% margin, down from 19.6%), profit DKK 1,544m after a DKK -823m discontinued-operations loss, FCF DKK 3,094m. A difficult year in which management cut the outlook twice; the share price fell 18.5% to DKK 215.2 against a C25 index up 2.7%.

Retail roll-up continued through the year: Ohrwerk Group (77 clinics, Germany, January), Amplifon's UK estate of ~100 directly operated clinics (~GBP 29m revenue, integrated into Hidden Hearing and completed in H1 2026), and Dansk Horecenter (36 clinics, acquired from GN).

Analyst sentiment improved through 2026. Consensus is around Buy/Hold with roughly 10 buy and 10 hold ratings among ~20 analysts and a mean target in the DKK 290-300 area (range ~DKK 245-330). BofA Securities upgraded from Underperform to Buy citing stronger-than-expected Q1 2026 market growth and faster traction for Oticon Zeal; Danske Bank raised its target to DKK 270 from DKK 230. Targets vary widely across sources, so treat any single figure with caution.

items.notes: Raised from 3-6% set with FY2025 results in February 2026. H1 delivered 7%.

Raised from DKK 4,100-4,500m. Midpoint DKK 4,600m implies ~16% growth on FY2025's DKK 3,960m and a full-year margin near 17.5-18%. H1 delivered DKK 2,134m, so guidance is skewed to H2 as cost savings land.
Explicitly zero for the full year while the group deleverages after KIND. No buybacks occurred in H1 2026 (versus DKK 582m in FY2025 and DKK 2,301m in FY2024).
Modelling assumption based on acquisitions completed as at 10 August 2026, up from 8% as at 2 February 2026.
Improved from -2%, based on rates as at 10 August 2026 including hedging.

items.metric: FX impact on EBIT before special items
items.notes: Improved from ~DKK -200m; impact expected to weigh slightly toward H2.

Increased cost, raised from DKK -325m: ~DKK 150m KIND transaction/integration (from 125m) plus DKK 250m one-off cost-saving severance and implementation costs (from 200m). A further ~DKK 100m of special items is still expected in 2027.
Raised from ~DKK 250m; ~DKK 100m realised in H1, ahead of plan; majority of the benefit lands in H2.

Raised from DKK 300m on better-than-expected performance and faster integration. KIND pro-forma revenue contribution ~DKK 2,000m (trimmed from an initial ~DKK 2,200m expectation due to weak 2025 market growth).

Previously assumed DKK -25m on Diagnostics; removed because management expects to recognise a refund in H2 of previously paid US tariffs. Management still flags elevated uncertainty in the global trade environment.

items.metric: Global hearing aid market value growth (assumption)
items.notes: Raised from 2-4%. Still described as conservative and below the 4-6% medium-to-long-term structural rate. Actual H1 2026 value growth was ~4%.
Management commentary; supported by continued favourable product and channel mix. H1 2026 was 77.1%.
Management commentary; in line with H1, while funding intensive investment in the Oticon Reveal launch and hearing care marketing.
3.0x at 30 June 2026, down from 3.4x at end-2025. Management reiterates a return to the 2.0-2.5x target range within 18-24 months of the KIND close (i.e. by roughly mid-2027).
Assumes 6-8% organic on ~5% assumed market growth, plus ~2% acquisitive.
In constant currencies. No absolute margin target is published.

items.target: Excess FCF after acquisitions to share buy-backs
items.notes: Subject to the 2.0-2.5x gearing target, which is why 2026 buybacks are zero. Demant pays no ordinary dividend.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Soren Nielsen framed 2025 as a challenging year in which the outlook was cut twice, but the fundamentals - ageing populations, sub-20% treatment penetration - were unchanged, and set out an ambitious 2026 profitability plan. At H1 2026 the tone is markedly more confident: organic growth of 7% was 'above our expectations', gross margin beat, cost savings are 'progressing ahead of plans', KIND is integrating faster than expected, and US market share is being regained on Oticon Zeal. Management explicitly cautions that the H2 outlook assumes several competitors will launch new products, and plans intensive investment behind the Oticon Reveal launch while holding organic OPEX growth near 5%. CAPEX has been running at ~3% of revenue.

bull_case: Genuine inflection after a bad 2025: organic growth swung from 0% in H1 2025 to 7% in H1 2026, EBIT before special items grew 19% in local currencies, and management raised FY2026 guidance twice-over on both lines (organic 3-6% to 6-7%; EBIT DKK 4,100-4,500m to DKK 4,400-4,800m). The midpoint implies ~16% EBIT growth on FY2025.

The product cycle is currently in Demant's favour and self-funding the next leg: Oticon Zeal drove double-digit North American organic growth and recovered share in both the US commercial market and the VA channel, reversing the specific 2025 share loss, while Oticon Reveal (dual-AI, orderable from 24 August 2026) provides a fresh premium platform for H2 2026 and 2027.

Three independent margin levers are compounding simultaneously: gross margin at 77.1% and guided above 77% on mix; a cost programme now worth ~DKK 300m to FY2026 EBIT and running ahead of plan; and KIND synergies worth DKK 325m in 2026 with full realisation only by end-2027 - meaning a meaningful part of the margin benefit has not yet landed in reported numbers.

Deleveraging is visibly on track and creates a capital-return option: gearing fell from 3.4x to 3.0x in six months on DKK 1,284m of H1 free cash flow (+14%), with NIBD down DKK 792m. A return to the 2.0-2.5x target by roughly mid-2027 would restart buybacks, which historically ran at DKK 0.6-3.2bn a year against a ~DKK 60bn market capitalisation - a material re-rating catalyst in a company that pays no dividend.

Structural demand is close to unarguable and barely tapped: over 400 million people have moderate-to-severe hearing loss, fewer than 20% of those who would benefit receive treatment, and half of the 4-6% structural market growth comes from demographics alone. Demant is one of five players controlling that market, and the tariff assumption has already been removed from guidance.

The portfolio is now clean: with EPOS sold (January 2026) and the implants exit finished (March 2026), the DKK -823m and DKK -504m discontinued-operations drags of 2025 and 2024 fall away, so group profit converges toward the DKK 2,367m continuing-operations figure - an earnings uplift that requires no operational improvement at all.
bear_case: The balance sheet is genuinely stretched and structurally so: DKK 17,950m of net debt against DKK 11,317m of equity, gearing at 3.0x versus a 2.0-2.5x target, ~DKK 750m of annual financial expense, and only ~half of next-twelve-months interest cost fixed or hedged. Because clinic roll-up is a permanent strategy, leverage and goodwill never normalise - total assets rose 20% in FY2025 almost entirely on acquisition goodwill, and any deterioration in clinic economics triggers impairment.

A large share of the growth is bought, not earned: acquisitions contributed 10 of the 15 percentage points of H1 2026 revenue growth and 9% of guided FY2026 growth. Stripping that out, the underlying business grows at 6-7% in a market Demant itself assumes will grow only 3-4% in value - a share-gain assumption that must be re-won every product cycle, and one Demant conspicuously failed to meet in 2025.

2025 showed how quickly this model breaks: two guidance cuts, EBIT margin down 240bp from 19.6% to 17.2%, a real US market-share loss to one large retailer, and an 18.5% share price fall against a C25 up 2.7%. Management explicitly warns that several competitors will launch new products in H2 2026 - Demant is currently at the most favourable and therefore most vulnerable point of its own cycle.

Structural price pressure from both ends of the channel: ASP fell 2% in FY2025 on geography and channel mix, management's own long-term base case is flat ASP, US managed care has posted negative growth for six consecutive quarters and is consolidating purchasing power among fewer, larger payers, and OTC/consumer-electronics entrants (Apple's FDA-cleared AirPods Pro hearing feature) anchor consumer price expectations at the low end even if prescription volumes are so far demonstrably unharmed.

No shareholder returns in 2026 and no dividend: guidance is explicitly zero buybacks for the full year, so the entire 2026 total return depends on multiple expansion. Against a share price that has already run from DKK 215.2 at end-2025 to DKK 285.40 (+33% year-to-date, near the 52-week high of ~DKK 290) on guidance upgrades, much of the recovery is arguably priced - the consensus target of roughly DKK 290-300 sits barely above the current price, and half of covering analysts rate it only Hold.

Governance offers minorities little leverage: the William Demant Foundation controls ~59% of share capital and intends to stay at 55-60%, so there is no realistic takeover premium, no activist path, and effective Foundation determination of the board - alongside a 2026 in which both the board chair changed and the Hearing Aids presidency passed to an external hire. Free float is 41% on average daily turnover of only DKK 66m, making the position hard to exit in size.

Demonstrated operational tail risk: the 2019 ransomware attack cost DKK 550-650m of EBIT, roughly 15% of that year's operating profit, from a single IT event in a group with a highly centralised value chain and now 26,616 employees across 4,500+ clinics - a far larger attack surface than in 2019.
